neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: No ptosis at rest. On sustained upgaze, subtle right ptosis at 80 seconds. No diplopia on casual testing. patient.chief_complaint: Progressive proximal leg weakness 6 months after completing SCLC chemotherapy
patient.history_present_illness: A 68-year-old woman with recently completed treatment for limited-stage small cell lung cancer presented with 3 months of progressive proximal leg weakness. She completed 4 cycles of carboplatin/etoposide chemotherapy with concurrent thoracic radiation 6 months ago and achieved a complete radiographic response. At her most recent surveillance visit, she reported difficulty rising from chairs — she now requires using both arm rests to push herself to standing — and difficulty climbing stairs. She initially attributed this to deconditioning after cancer treatment. Her oncologist referred her to rehabilitation, which helped minimally. She has also noted intermittent double vision when driving and reading, occurring in the afternoons but not in the mornings. She mentioned her mouth seems dry most of the time. Over the past 3 months, she has had mild difficulty chewing and her voice becomes nasal in the evenings. She denies sensory symptoms in her hands but has mild numbness in her feet (known carboplatin neuropathy). She denies dysphagia, ptosis in the morning, or respiratory symptoms. Her oncologist ordered a brain MRI and PET-CT which showed no cancer recurrence. She was referred to neurology with the working diagnosis of either carboplatin peripheral neuropathy or paraneoplastic syndrome from SCLC.

specialized_test.test_type: EMG, NCS, and Repetitive Nerve Stimulation

findings.significance: Reduced baseline CMAP in lower extremity — suggestive of pre-synaptic disorder
Reduced baseline CMAP — pre-synaptic NMJ disorder vs platinum neuropathy
PATHOLOGICAL FACILITATION — indicates a pre-synaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission

findings.result: Baseline 0.9 mV increases to 2.2 mV after 10-second MVC
findings.significance: Post-exercise facilitation — pre-synaptic NMJ disorder pattern

specialized_test.impression: Low baseline CMAP amplitudes (deltoid 0.9 mV; reference >3 mV) with 118% CMAP increment on 50 Hz repetitive nerve stimulation, exceeding the >100% threshold. Post-exercise facilitation demonstrated (baseline 0.9 mV increasing to 2.2 mV after brief maximum voluntary contraction). No pathological low-frequency decremental response. Superimposed axonal sensory neuropathy on sensory NCS. The electrophysiological findings indicate a pre-synaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission (low baseline CMAP with high-rate facilitation and post-exercise repair), in contrast to a post-synaptic pattern. Clinical correlation and serological evaluation recommended.
recommended_actions: Correlation with neuromuscular antibody studies recommended.
Further clinical and imaging evaluation as directed.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS), paraneoplastic, secondary to recurrent small cell lung cancer; anti-VGCC P/Q positive, anti-SOX1 positive

differential.key_features: MG produces fatigable ocular/bulbar weakness with normal baseline CMAP and decrement; here baseline CMAP low with facilitation pattern; AChR negative.
Etoposide/carboplatin can cause weakness but not >100% RNS facilitation.
Could explain mild sensory findings but not pre-synaptic NMJ facilitation pattern.
Prior thoracic radiation could cause brachial plexopathy but does not produce symmetric proximal LE weakness with facilitation.

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Anti-VGCC P/Q positive and anti-SOX1 positive confirm LEMS with paraneoplastic mechanism; AChR negative

critical_actions: PET-CT for SCLC recurrence after standard CT
Oncology referral for SCLC recurrence staging and treatment
Initiate amifampridine after ECG and drug-interaction review
Coordinate with palliative care given prior SCLC history
contraindicated_actions: Do NOT diagnose this as MG — pre-synaptic facilitation pattern and anti-VGCC positivity place this in LEMS.
Do NOT prescribe aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, IV magnesium, NMBs.
Do NOT defer oncology workup pending serology — paraneoplastic syndromes often precede radiographic recurrence.
key_reasoning_points: Proximal weakness improving with brief exercise (post-activation facilitation) is the LEMS signature — opposite of MG.
Anti-VGCC P/Q positive in 85-90% of LEMS; anti-SOX1 strongly indicates SCLC.
Standard CT may miss small recurrent SCLC; PET-CT is the imaging of choice.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Conclude 'NMJ disorder excluded' and miss LEMS.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: AChR-negative does not exclude LEMS; anti-VGCC is the discriminating test.

red_herrings.data_point: CT chest post-treatment changes without new mass
red_herrings.intended_effect: Reassurance that SCLC is in remission and stop oncology workup.
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Standard CT has limited sensitivity for small recurrence; PET-CT is required; LEMS often precedes radiographic recurrence by months.
